Why Tencent Chases AI Revenue. And Not Profits (Yet)

I was just in China visiting Tencent.

And my take-away was that Tencent spotted the AI pricing trap early. 

Here are my 3 take-aways:

Note: I have a full podcast episode on this. Link below.

Point 1: AI has a variable cost problem that traditional software never had.

An agent can use way more AI and compute than a human user.

And this increases even more when you go to multi-agent. 

Point 2: Tencent anchors its agent strategy on high value, scalable use cases.

It started with WorkBuddy for work productivity

And CodeBuddy for coding.

Next up is design. Watch for Ardot and Miora.

Point 3: The big KPIs are market share, growth and incremental revenue.

Profit is not a big KPI (yet)

But revenue must cover AI's variable costs.

Other scaling is pretty bad. See Grok Bot right now.

***Takeaways for Managers:

Takeaway 1: Pull last month’s AI usage bill and see which teams drive the cost.

Takeaway 2: Ask your AI vendors how pricing changes when agents run all day.

We’re going to have 100X more agents in the enterprise working with our data and systems than even people do today. Every AI agent deployment comes down to how successfully they can get access to the critical context to make a decision, do research, or execute tasks. 

90% of the data in an enterprise is unstructured data, which means this critical context is living inside of our documents, contracts, marketing assets, research materials, financial plans, design files, and more. Which means we need effective ways for agents to get access to this critical enterprise content to other work.

We’re excited to partner with NVIDIA to deliver advanced context retrieval -combining lexical and semantic search in Box- to ensure that AI agents can find the most relevant information they’re looking for. All in a way that adheres to their enterprise security, access controls, and data governance policies, so agents only work with the data they’re allowed to.

fullText:
你想让AI自动筛选出美食网站上所有“健康食品”的照片，有时候AI搞不准，这是因为你也没把标准搞清晰

比如你告诉AI，找出所有健康食品

AI开始分类，边界清晰的容易判断，但有些东西未必有唯一正确答案，你也没说清楚所谓的“健康”究竟是指什么

于是你不得不一遍一遍改提示词

谷歌开源了一个AI分类框架：Agile Deliberation，让AI主动寻找那些难以判断的边界案例，反过来帮助人们把模糊的判断标准变成明确可执行的分类规则

简单说，就是AI的角色变了

过去你告诉AI什么是对的，现在AI帮你发现，你自己究竟认为什么是对的

等你的标准越来越清楚，AI再据此优化分类规则

整个流程有两个核心阶段：
Concept Scoping，界定概念范围
先把模糊概念拆开，明确应该包含哪些情况，排除哪些情况，建立初步分类规则

Concept Iteration，迭代分类标准
AI主动去找容易产生争议的边界图片，让用户判断是否符合当前分类标准

然后系统根据反馈不断调整分类指令，再去找新的边界案例，直到规则逐渐符合用户真正想表达的标准

这个框架有几个非常应景的场景

平台内容审核，比如说什么样的广告属于误导性宣传？让AI找出有争议的案例，审核人员判断，完善审核规则

另外一个，企业数据标注，比如什么样的商品照片算高质量，什么样的广告素材符合品牌风格，AI可以通过边界案例帮助建立更一致的判断标准
